teams.heading: Planet Rugby expects France to hammer Jake White's Fiji in Lyon
teams.body: Planet Rugby's preview says France will use their attacking game to beat Jake White's side in Lyon, while risking a 'soft underbelly' before the South Africa test six days later. The news behind it is the selection: Antoine Dupont and Romain Ntamack start together at half-back for the first time since March 2025, a 20-month gap, with Matthieu Jalibert out injured. For Fiji, the piece recalls Mick Byrne leaving in April and Senirusi Seruvakula serving as interim coach through July before White was appointed.

lead.why: Every NEW item fails the Fiji test: #1 is an Ireland match report that only mentions Fiji in its headline, and #2 is a broadcast guide about France, so the Planet Rugby preview stands as the only Fiji

teams.heading: RFU's Bill Sweeney gives Steve Borthwick unequivocal backing before Australia test
teams.body: This week RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney gave Steve Borthwick his unequivocal backing to lead England at the 2027 World Cup. It follows the union's decision two months ago to extend the head coach's contract until after the 2028 Six Nations, even though England lost four of five matches in a single championship for the first time. Sweeney said: "We're committed to Steve. We believe in what he's doing." England have lost five of their last seven Tests, and Sweeney added that the union wants "continued progress".

lead.why: A formal union endorsement of England's head coach is new, England-specific business, and it avoids the Furbank, George and Atkinson stories already reported.

teams.heading: France v Fiji streams free on TF1+, ITVX and RugbyPass TV
teams.body: Les Bleus' Saturday meeting with Fiji in Lyon can be watched without a subscription in four markets. In France it is on TF1+ and broadcast channel TF1; in the UK, ITV1 and ITVX both carry it, though viewers need a current TV Licence to watch live television. Ireland gets it on Virgin Media Play and Virgin Media One, and in the United States it is on World Rugby's RugbyPass TV, which requires registration before streaming.

lead.why: It is the only new France item in the shortlist, as the team selection has already been covered today.

teams.heading: Robert Baloucoune goes off with knock as Mack Hansen has ankle concern
teams.body: Robert Baloucoune departed in the 58th minute of Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina, one of several knocks picked up in Dublin. Mack Hansen continued after treatment but has an ankle concern, as does Josh van der Flier, while Sean Jansen sustained a "bang" to his knee. The knocks are particularly concerning for Andy Farrell's back three, who had played together only once before and produced Hugo Keenan's first try after Baloucoune found Hansen in space. Keenan, Hansen and Baloucoune have all struggled with injuries in the past year.

lead.why: It carries fresh match-day injury news on Baloucoune, Hansen and others, distinct from the Sheehan story already run.

teams.heading: Italy crumble to 66-7 defeat as Springboks run in nine tries
teams.body: Italy lost 66-7 to South Africa on Saturday, conceding nine tries, their fourth straight defeat, and were 45-0 down at half-time. Head coach Gonzalo Quesada's side went into the match without 16 players, including captain Michele Lamaro and centres Tommaso Menoncello and Juan Ignacio Brex. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu was the Springboks' standout, scoring a solo try and kicking 21 points, while the world champions moved alone to the top of the Southern Hemisphere standings.

lead.why: It is a new match-result item on Italy's defeat, the fresh event the day's edition should centre on, rather than the post-match quotes already covered.

teams.heading: Ewan Ashman hat-trick not enough as Scotland fade against All Blacks
teams.body: Ewan Ashman's three first-half tries gave Scotland a chance at Murrayfield, but the hooker's hat-trick was the lone high point of a day that slipped away after the interval. Scotland failed to score in the second half as New Zealand added three tries, one from Beauden Barrett, and Planet Rugby noted Ashman became the first Scotsman to score a hat-trick against the All Blacks. Head coach Gregor Townsend said: "And it wasn't there today. So that's frustrating." Scotland's next match is against Australia.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy admits Wales need vast improvement despite Japan win
teams.body: Wales had to hold on in Cardiff, beating Japan 28-21 for a bonus-point win and their second of the autumn. Archie Griffin opened the scoring inside four minutes, and Josh Adams went on to score twice, with Louis Rees-Zammit also over. Kenta Fukuda's 75th-minute try kept Japan within a score until Adams claimed a turnover penalty with seconds left. It was Tandy's fourth win in 13 Tests in charge, watched by a sparse crowd at the Millennium Stadium.

lead.why: Wales' head coach's own post-match admission is a fresh team story that goes beyond the match report already run.

teams.heading: Pumas captain Julián Montoya fails head injury assessment in Dublin loss
teams.body: Julián Montoya went off for a head injury assessment 28 minutes into the Dublin defeat and never returned, with BBC Sport reporting that the Pumas captain failed the HIA before half-time. Leonel Oviedo also went through an HIA, returning to the field after about four minutes, and the Americas Rugby News report describes the forwards as repeatedly disrupted. Argentina travel to Italy and France next, after a third defeat in four games.

lead.why: A new injury to the captain, a different thread from the yellow cards already covered, and a fresh report on the forward disruption.

teams.heading: Rugby Australia writes directly to Wallabies players over pay, bypassing union
teams.body: Negotiations for a new collective agreement are not going well, and the Wallabies are heading into Sunday's Test with the dispute unresolved. Rupa president Tom Robertson said he was disappointed the offer went straight to players, "particularly while the Wallabies are on tour". Rugby Australia chair Daniel Herbert responded that Rupa's counter-proposals "threaten the future of the game in Australia". The two Bledisloe Cup defeats by New Zealand were the last Tests under the 2023 agreement.

lead.why: Items #1 and #2 are NEW but are about England, failing the 'genuinely about Australia' test, so #4 is the strongest Australia story not already run, with fresh Rugby Australia and Rupa exchanges.

teams.heading: Japan lose 21-28 in Cardiff as Shinya Komura's late try falls short
teams.body: Japan were left to rue missed chances at the Principality Stadium, where Wales had never lost to them. Ben Gunter and Warner Dearn scored for the Brave Blossoms, but Josh Adams' two tries, plus scores from Archie Griffin and Louis Rees-Zammit, were enough for Wales. Shinya Komura's try four minutes from time made it a one-score game. Eddie Jones said: "100 per cent. That could have been a historic win for us."

teams.heading: All Blacks shrug off Ewan Ashman's hat-trick, Scotland scoreless after the break
teams.body: Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman scored three first-half tries at Murrayfield, but New Zealand controlled the second half, when Scotland failed to score at all. Beauden Barrett scored two of the visitors' seven tries, Josh Moorby and Asafo Aumua added others, and Planet Rugby reports Ashman became the first Scotsman to score a hat-trick against the All Blacks. Wallace Sititi scored early but was yellow-carded in the first half.

teams.heading: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu stars as Springboks run in nine tries against Italy
teams.body: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu set the tone early, with a penalty and then a one-handed solo try, as the Springboks led 45-0 at half-time in Turin on Saturday. They finished 66-7 winners over an injury-hit Italy. Malcolm Marx scored twice, and Morné van den Berg, Siya Kolisi, Damian Willemse, Wilco Louw, Paul de Villiers and Ethan Hooker also crossed. It was a fourth straight bonus-point win in the Nations Championship, leaving South Africa alone on top of the Southern Hemisphere standings before the trip to face France in Paris.

lead.why: A new result from Turin, reported by two outlets, and the strongest fresh South Africa item on the shortlist.
